title: Advanced Java: sealed classes, records, pattern matching, modules, reflection
shortTitle: Advanced Java: sealed classes, records, pattern matching, modules, reflection
keyPoints: Sealed classes restrict which types may implement an interface, enabling exhaustive switch expressions without a default branch.
Records are immutable data carriers with auto-generated constructor, getters, equals, hashCode, and toString, ideal for API response DTOs.
Pattern matching combines type checking and variable binding in one step, eliminating manual casting in instanceof and switch blocks.
The Java Platform Module System (JPMS) declares explicit exports and dependencies, enforcing encapsulation at the jar level.
Reflection inspects classes at runtime, which is how Spring and Jackson read annotations, but it bypasses compile-time safety.
Combining sealed interfaces with records and pattern matching produces type-safe, exhaustive domain models for banking APIs.

s1_definition.oneliner: Sealed classes restrict a type hierarchy, records provide immutable DTOs, pattern matching eliminates casts, modules enforce encapsulation, and reflection powers frameworks – together they build type-safe, modern banking APIs.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Sealed classes** – restrict exactly which types may extend a class or implement an interface using the `sealed` and `permits` keywords, so the compiler knows every subtype and can enforce exhaustive `switch` expressions.
- **Records** – declared with `record`, they are immutable data carriers that auto-generate the canonical constructor, accessor methods, `equals`, `hashCode`, and `toString`, making them ideal for DTOs.
- **Pattern matching** – combines a type test and a variable binding in one step, available in `instanceof` (Java 16+) and `switch` expressions (Java 21+), removing manual casts.
- **JPMS modules** – declared in `module-info.java`, they enforce explicit `exports` and `requires` so internal packages are truly hidden at compile time and runtime.
- **Reflection** – the `java.lang.reflect` API inspects classes, methods, and fields at runtime, powering frameworks like Spring and Jackson but bypassing compile-time checks.
s1_definition.analogy: At National Bank of India, sealed classes are like the rule that only three approved departments – Savings, Current, and Loan – may handle account creation; no rogue department can sneak in. Records are the pre-printed receipt slips that are filled once and cannot be altered. Pattern matching is the smart teller window that reads the slip type and routes it in one step without asking twice. Modules are the locked office doors that only open to authorised departments. Reflection is the security camera that can see inside any office at runtime.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Sealed Interface: FeeStrategy
  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  sealed interface FeeStrategy           │
  │  permits:                               │
  │    ├── RegularFeeStrategy  (record)     │
  │    ├── PremiumFeeStrategy  (record)     │
  │    └── ZeroFeeStrategy     (record)     │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────┘
             │
             ▼
  switch (strategy) {
    case RegularFeeStrategy r  → 0.5%
    case PremiumFeeStrategy p  → 0.2%
    case ZeroFeeStrategy z     → 0
    // no default needed – exhaustive
  }
```

```text
  Module Encapsulation:
  ┌──────────────────────────────────┐
  │  module com.bank.service         │
  │                                  │
  │  exports com.bank.dto     ──────┼──→ visible to other modules
  │  exports com.bank.service ──────┼──→ visible to other modules
  │                                  │
  │  com.bank.model (not exported) ──┼──✗ hidden from other modules
  │  com.bank.internal              ──┼──✗ hidden from other modules
  └──────────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Modern Java gives API designers five powerful features that work together. Sealed classes restrict a type hierarchy to a known set of subtypes, so the compiler enforces exhaustive handling. Records provide immutable, boilerplate-free data carriers that serialize cleanly to JSON, making them ideal for DTOs. Pattern matching eliminates manual casts by combining type checks and variable binding in one step. Modules enforce true encapsulation at the JAR level, keeping internal classes hidden. And reflection, used by frameworks like Spring and Jackson, inspects classes at runtime to read annotations and populate fields.

The real power emerges when these features combine. At National Bank of India, Pankaj modelled transaction results as a sealed interface with three record subtypes: Success, InsufficientFunds, and AccountFrozen. The service returns this sealed result, the controller handles every case with a pattern-matching switch, and the compiler guarantees no case is missed. When the team later added a new result type for rate-limited transactions, the compiler immediately flagged every switch that did not handle the new case, catching the gap at build time rather than in production.

For DTOs, records replaced dozens of verbose response classes. An `AccountResponse` record with three components gives Rajesh exactly the fields he should see, serializes to JSON with Jackson out of the box since version 2.12, and cannot be mutated after creation. The module system ensures that internal entity classes in `com.bank.model` are never accidentally imported by another team's microservice, even if the classes are public.

Remember one sentence: sealed classes define what types exist, records carry the data immutably, pattern matching dispatches exhaustively, modules hide the internals, and reflection lets frameworks wire it all together.
